name: On-prem infrastructure design and build
summary: Servers, storage and networking designed and built in your own rooms or racks, on VMware or Proxmox, and handed over documented.
deliverables: A written design covering capacity, networking, storage and backup
Hypervisor hosts installed and configured, on VMware vSphere or Proxmox VE
Virtual networks, VLANs and storage set up and tested
Backup, restore and failover tested end to end
Monitoring and alerting for hosts and virtual machines
Runbook and handover session for your own team
fit: Organisations that want to run their own virtualised infrastructure on premises, or move off an ageing or costly platform, with a design they can trust.
needs: Your current kit and workloads if any, the number of virtual machines you expect, and your uptime and backup expectations.

research.headline: Your own virtualised compute and storage, built to last.
research.scenario: A research group has servers and storage but each one is configured by hand. We design a clustered, backed-up virtual environment on Proxmox or VMware, with shared storage and clear access for students and staff.
deliverables: A written design sized to your workloads and growth
Hypervisor cluster on Proxmox VE or VMware vSphere
Shared storage and networks separated by project
Backup and restore tested for data you cannot lose
Monitoring and alerting for hosts and virtual machines
A runbook a new postdoc or student can follow
research.fit: Research groups and labs that run their own servers and need them consolidated, reliable and documented.
research.needs: A list of current servers and storage, the workloads you run and who needs access.
research.priceNote: Smaller: a single site with a few hosts. Larger: clustered storage, GPU hosts or many projects with separate networks.

startup.headline: Own your infrastructure instead of renting it forever.
startup.scenario: A startup with steady workloads finds cloud bills growing faster than revenue. We design and build a small on-premises or colocated virtual platform, with backup and a path to burst into the cloud.
deliverables: A cost comparison and design for an on-prem or colocated platform
Hypervisor hosts on Proxmox VE or VMware vSphere
Networking, firewalling and remote access
Backup and recovery tested against realistic failures
Monitoring and a simple capacity plan
Documentation so a small team can run it
startup.fit: Teams with predictable workloads who want lower running costs and control over their data.
startup.needs: Your workloads and their size, where the hardware will live and your budget range for equipment.
startup.priceNote: Smaller: two or three hosts in one room. Larger: high availability, multiple sites or strict recovery targets.

regulated.headline: Infrastructure that keeps data on premises, and can be explained to an auditor.
regulated.scenario: A firm must keep client data in its own premises. We design a segmented, backed-up virtual environment with access control and logging, documented in terms an auditor can follow.
deliverables: A written design with network segmentation and access control
Hypervisor cluster on VMware vSphere or Proxmox VE
Encrypted storage and tested backups held off site
Central logging and alerting
A recovery plan with tested restore times
Documentation for audits and for your own staff
regulated.fit: Law, health and finance firms that need data held on premises with clear controls and records.
regulated.needs: Your data and compliance requirements, current systems and recovery expectations.
regulated.priceNote: Smaller: one office with a few hosts. Larger: two sites, high availability or detailed audit evidence.

msp.headline: A hosting platform your team can build services on, or a way off VMware costs.
msp.scenario: An IT provider wants a platform for hosting client workloads, or needs to move clients off VMware after licensing changes. We design the target platform, build it and plan the migration.
deliverables: A platform design for multi-client hosting or migration
Build on Proxmox VE or VMware vSphere
Tenant networks, storage and role-based access
Migration plan and pilot move of selected virtual machines
Backup, monitoring and capacity reporting
Runbooks for your engineers
msp.fit: Managed service providers building or replacing a virtualisation platform for client workloads.
msp.needs: Your current estate, number of clients and virtual machines, and any licensing deadline.
msp.priceNote: Smaller: a pilot platform and a few machines. Larger: many tenants, high availability or a full estate migration.

name: Cloud landing zone
summary: An Azure or AWS foundation written in Terraform: networking, identity, logging and cost controls.
deliverables: Terraform modules in your own repository
Network layout: virtual networks, subnets and security rules
Identity and access baseline, with least-privilege roles
Central logging and budget alerts
A handover session and a written runbook
fit: Teams whose cloud account was built by hand and now needs to be repeatable and safe to change.
needs: Cloud account access and a list of the workloads you plan to run.

startup.headline: A cloud account you can grow into, set up in your first month instead of your first crisis.
startup.scenario: A seed-stage team has been deploying to an AWS or Azure account by hand, with shared logins and no record of what is running. We rebuild the foundation as code, separate development from production and add cost alerts, so your first hires inherit something safe.
deliverables: Separate development, staging and production accounts or subscriptions
Terraform modules for networking, identity and shared services, in your repository
Single sign-on and role-based access instead of shared credentials
Budget alerts and tagging, so the cost of each environment is visible
A layout your CI/CD pipeline can deploy into without admin rights
A recorded walkthrough and runbook for new engineers
startup.fit: Seed to Series A teams about to hire their first engineers, or about to answer a customer's security questionnaire.
startup.needs: Admin access to the current account, a list of the services in use and the order you expect to launch environments.
startup.priceNote: Smaller: one cloud and two environments. Larger: several regions, existing resources to import or a customer security review to answer.

regulated.headline: A cloud foundation built around who can see what, with the evidence to show it.
regulated.scenario: A small firm is moving a line-of-business system to the cloud and needs to explain to clients where data lives and who can reach it. We design the network and access model first, log everything that matters and document the data flows for your data protection lead.
deliverables: Deployment in a UK region, with data residency choices written down
Private networking, with no public access to data stores by default
Role design with least privilege and mandatory multi-factor sign-in
Central audit logging with a retention period you choose
Encryption settings documented for data at rest and in transit
A data-flow diagram and control summary for your data protection lead
regulated.fit: Law firms, clinics, accountants and advisers moving client or patient information to the cloud.
regulated.needs: The systems and data types involved, any client or contract security requirements and a named person responsible for data protection.
regulated.priceNote: Larger where long audit retention, extra environments or client-specific control requirements apply. We document the controls, but compliance itself stays your responsibility.

msp.headline: A repeatable cloud baseline you can offer to more than one client.
msp.scenario: An IT provider keeps rebuilding similar Azure or AWS setups for small clients, each slightly different. We turn your best version into a parameterised Terraform baseline, so the next client takes days instead of weeks.
deliverables: A parameterised Terraform baseline for a typical small-business tenancy
Guardrails for naming, tagging, policy and budget alerts, applied the same way every time
Separate state and access for each client
A pull-request workflow, so your engineers review every change
A deployment checklist and handover pack you can reuse
A training session on running and extending the code
msp.fit: Providers with several small clients on Azure or AWS who want consistency and fewer one-off builds.
msp.needs: An example of your current client build, your tenancy and billing model, and how many client types you expect.
msp.priceNote: Smaller: one client type on one cloud. Larger: several client profiles, or migration of existing client builds.

name: Kubernetes baseline
summary: A hardened cluster with ingress, TLS and monitoring, ready for your first workloads.
deliverables: Cluster build, managed or self-hosted, defined as code
Ingress and automatic TLS certificates
Hardening to a baseline we agree with you
Prometheus and Grafana monitoring with starter dashboards
A worked example deployment and a runbook
fit: Teams moving from single servers to containers, or taking over a cluster nobody fully understands.
needs: Details of the applications to run and where the cluster will live.

startup.headline: A cluster your team can deploy to on day one, without hiring a platform engineer.
startup.scenario: A product team has outgrown a couple of servers and deploys containers by hand. We stand up a managed cluster, set up ingress and certificates, and give developers one clear way to ship a service.
deliverables: A managed cluster on your chosen cloud, defined in Terraform
Ingress and automatic TLS certificates
Namespaces and resource limits for each team or environment
A deployment template for a new service, with health checks
Prometheus and Grafana, with alerts for the failures that wake people up
A cost and scaling note, so the first bill is no surprise
startup.fit: Startups running three or more services, or planning to, with developers but no dedicated operations engineer.
startup.needs: Your services and how they are built today, your preferred cloud and the traffic you expect.
startup.priceNote: Smaller: a managed cluster and two environments. Larger: stateful services, several clusters or a service mesh.

research.headline: Containers for reproducible research, on the hardware you already have.
research.scenario: A group wants to run analysis pipelines and models in containers so results can be repeated, on a small on-premises cluster or a few GPU machines. We build a cluster that fits the hardware and the way researchers work.
deliverables: A cluster on your own servers or a university cloud allocation
GPU scheduling, so notebooks and jobs can request a card
Shared storage mounted into workloads, with quotas
A container registry and a worked example for one of your own pipelines
Monitoring of node, GPU and storage use, with a simple usage report
A guide for researchers in plain language
research.fit: Research groups moving analysis and model training into containers, or sharing a few GPU machines between people.
research.needs: Hardware details, the software and datasets involved and how many people will use it.
research.priceNote: Smaller: a single small cluster. Larger: GPU scheduling, large shared storage or integration with a university login.

msp.headline: A hardened cluster you can run for a client without owning every decision.
msp.scenario: A provider has a client who wants Kubernetes, but nobody on the team has run it in production. We build and harden the cluster to a written baseline and leave runbooks your engineers can follow.
deliverables: A cluster built to a written hardening baseline
Role-based access mapped to your engineers and the client's staff
Backup and restore for cluster state and one example workload
Monitoring and alert routing into your existing tools
An upgrade plan and a tested first upgrade
A runbook and handover session for your support team
msp.fit: IT providers supporting a client's first production cluster, or taking over one with no documentation.
msp.needs: The client's requirements, your ticketing and alerting tools, and who will provide support after handover.
msp.priceNote: Larger where backup, upgrade testing or integration with your tools is included. Support after handover is scoped separately.

name: CI/CD pipeline
summary: Automated build, test and deploy, so releases stop depending on one person's laptop.
deliverables: Pipeline in GitHub Actions or Jenkins, whichever suits your team
Containerised builds with Docker
Separate staging and production environments
Secrets handling and a documented rollback step
Short written guide for your developers
fit: Small engineering teams that deploy by hand and want faster, safer releases.
needs: Repository access and a description of how you release today.

startup.headline: Releases that take minutes and do not depend on one person.
startup.scenario: A small team deploys by copying files or running scripts from a laptop, and every release is a stressful event. We build a pipeline that tests, packages and deploys on every merge, with a clear way back if something breaks.
deliverables: A pipeline in GitHub Actions or Jenkins, matched to your team
Automated tests and linting on every pull request
Containerised builds with caching to keep them fast
Staging deploys on merge and production deploys on approval
Secrets stored safely, with no keys in the repository
A documented rollback and a one-page guide for developers
startup.fit: Startups with two to ten developers who want faster, safer releases and fewer late-night deployments.
startup.needs: Repository access, a description of how you release today and the hosting you deploy to.
startup.priceNote: Smaller: one application and one pipeline. Larger: several services, database migrations or mobile app builds.

msp.headline: A pipeline template you can reuse across client projects.
msp.scenario: An IT provider supports software for several clients, each deployed differently. We build one standard pipeline with client-specific settings, so builds, tests and deployments follow a single process.
deliverables: Reusable pipeline templates with per-client settings
Per-client secrets and permissions kept separate
Approval steps that match each client's change process
Deployment logs kept as part of your change records
A starter repository and onboarding checklist for new clients
Training for your engineers on adapting the templates
msp.fit: Providers delivering or supporting applications for several clients who want one consistent release process.
msp.needs: Two or three example client projects, your change-approval rules and your preferred tooling.
msp.priceNote: Larger: several client templates, approval workflows or a move from Jenkins to GitHub Actions.

name: Linux estate automation
summary: Ansible roles that build, patch and harden your Linux servers the same way every time.
deliverables: Ansible roles for builds, patching and hardening
An inventory and tests so changes can be checked before they run
Patch status reporting you can show an auditor
A Git workflow for reviewing configuration changes
A runbook for your own team
fit: Organisations running a mix of Red Hat, Rocky, Ubuntu and older systems, patched by hand.
needs: A server list, access to a test machine and your current patching rules.

research.headline: One tested way to build and patch every research server, whatever its distribution.
research.scenario: A research computing team looks after a mix of Rocky, Red Hat and Ubuntu machines built over several years, with scientific software installed by hand. We capture the standard build in Ansible so new nodes match, and patching becomes planned instead of improvised.
deliverables: Ansible roles for the base build, users, storage mounts and monitoring agents
Support for several distributions in one codebase
Scientific software environments managed as code where practical
Staged patching, with a test group first and a rollback note
Reports on patch status and pending reboots
A runbook and a Git workflow for reviewing changes
research.fit: Research computing teams and labs with a mixed fleet of servers and a small support team.
research.needs: A server list, access to a test machine and the software your researchers depend on.
research.priceNote: Smaller: one distribution and a small fleet. Larger: several distributions, software environments to capture or many nodes.

regulated.headline: Patching and hardening you can show an auditor.
regulated.scenario: A firm has to evidence that its servers are patched and configured to a standard, and currently relies on spreadsheets and memory. We write the standard into Ansible and produce the reports from the same run.
deliverables: Hardening roles aligned to a baseline you choose, such as the CIS Benchmarks
Scheduled patching with maintenance windows and an approval step
Evidence reports: what was patched, when and on which servers
Drift checks that flag servers which have moved away from the standard
Access and logging settings applied consistently
A change history in Git that records who approved what
regulated.fit: Regulated businesses with a Linux estate and a duty to show that systems are patched and secured.
regulated.needs: A server list, your patching policy or client requirements and the person who approves change.
regulated.priceNote: Larger: large estates, several distributions or detailed evidence reporting. We build to the baseline you select but do not certify compliance.

msp.headline: Fewer one-off fixes and a cleaner patching routine across client estates.
msp.scenario: A provider patches client Linux servers by hand, with different scripts for each client. We build shared Ansible roles with a separate inventory per client, so patching runs the same way everywhere and reports are produced automatically.
deliverables: Shared Ansible roles with a separate inventory for each client
Patch windows per client and a staged rollout order
Pre-checks and post-checks, with failures raised in your ticketing system
A monthly patch report you can send to each client
Build roles for the server types you provision most often
Training and a runbook for your engineers
msp.fit: Providers managing Linux servers for several clients, with scripts and habits that differ from engineer to engineer.
msp.needs: Access to a representative client estate, your ticketing system and your current patching steps.
msp.priceNote: Larger: many client estates, ticketing integration or custom reporting.

name: HPC and GPU cluster setup
summary: Slurm scheduling, shared storage and GPU support for a research group or lab.
deliverables: Slurm scheduler set up and tuned for your workloads
Shared storage layout and user accounts
GPU drivers and a container runtime for researchers
Monitoring and usage reports
A user guide written for scientists, not administrators
fit: Research groups with new or shared compute and nobody on staff to run it.
needs: Hardware details, the software your researchers use and the number of users.

research.headline: A shared compute system that scientists can use and your team can run.
research.scenario: A group has bought or been given GPU servers and a storage array, and everyone is logging in with shared accounts and competing for the same cards. We set up Slurm with fair-share rules, a storage layout with quotas and the software environments people need.
deliverables: A Slurm scheduler with partitions, limits and fair-share rules for your groups
GPU drivers, CUDA and container support for reproducible jobs
A storage layout for home, project and scratch areas, with quotas
User accounts, login or single sign-on, and onboarding steps
Software environments, as modules or containers, for your main tools
Monitoring of queues, GPU use and storage, with a usage report for funders
A user guide for researchers and a runbook for administrators
research.fit: Research groups and labs with new or shared compute and nobody employed to run it.
research.needs: A hardware list and network layout, the software and datasets in use, the number of users and how time should be shared fairly.
research.priceNote: Smaller: a handful of nodes. Larger: many nodes, high-speed networking, large shared storage or a move from an existing scheduler.

name: Private AI pilot
summary: A language model running on your own infrastructure, tested on one real use case.
deliverables: A self-hosted language model on your servers or in your private cloud
Access controls and audit logging
One use case tested against your own documents
A human approval step before the AI changes anything
A usage guide and a plan for what comes after the pilot
fit: Teams that want AI on sensitive information without sending it to a third-party service.
needs: One clear use case, sample documents and a decision-maker for data access.

regulated.headline: Try AI on client documents without those documents leaving your control.
regulated.scenario: A practice wants to summarise and search long documents, such as contracts or case files, but cannot send them to a public AI service. We run a model inside your environment, limit who can use it, log what it does and test it on one real task.
deliverables: A self-hosted model on your servers or in a UK private cloud
Document search limited to the folders and people you approve
Per-person access and an audit log of the questions asked
A human review step before anything is saved, sent or changed
A test on one real task, compared with how your staff do it today
A data-flow note for your data protection lead and a plan for what comes after the pilot
regulated.fit: Law firms, clinics, accountants and advisers who want AI on client or patient information.
regulated.needs: One task, sample documents you are allowed to use and a person who can approve data access.
regulated.priceNote: Larger: several document sources, stricter access rules or dedicated GPU hardware. Hardware is a separate cost, and we help you size it before you buy.

startup.headline: Build an AI feature on infrastructure you control, before you commit to a vendor.
startup.scenario: A startup wants an AI assistant over its own data, but customers keep asking where their data goes. We deploy an open-weight model, test retrieval over your content and show what quality and cost look like with self-hosting.
deliverables: An open-weight model served through an API your product can call
Retrieval over your documents or knowledge base, with a test set
Quality results on your own questions, not generic benchmarks
Cost and speed per request on the hardware used
Authentication, rate limits and logging at the API
A written comparison with a hosted service, ending in a clear recommendation
startup.fit: Startups adding AI to a product where customers care about data location, or where hosted per-use costs may become high.
startup.needs: The product feature you have in mind, sample content and the number of users or requests you expect.
startup.priceNote: Larger: several data sources, an agent that takes actions or load testing at scale.

research.headline: Run language models on unpublished or restricted data, on hardware you own.
research.scenario: A group wants to use a language model on unpublished results or restricted datasets that cannot leave the institution. We deploy a model on your GPU servers, connect it to a collection of papers or data descriptions and test it on one research task.
deliverables: A model deployed on your GPU servers, sharing capacity fairly with other work
Search over your own papers, notes or data descriptions
Access limited to the project team, with usage logged
A test on one research task, with errors recorded for review
A reproducible setup, with model versions and settings recorded
A short report you can reuse in ethics or data-governance discussions
research.fit: Research groups with restricted or unpublished data, and spare GPU capacity or a budget to get some.
research.needs: The research task, the data rules that apply and details of your GPU hardware.
research.priceNote: Smaller if suitable GPUs are already in place. Larger: new hardware setup or integration with an existing cluster.

name: Application development
summary: A custom web or mobile app, designed, built and launched in agreed phases, on infrastructure we set up properly.
deliverables: A written scope and a clickable design before any code is written
Web application, mobile app or both, built in short stages with weekly demos
Back end, database and APIs, with automated tests
Hosting, deployment pipeline and monitoring set up for you
Source code in your own repository, with a handover guide
Optional support after launch
fit: Teams with a clear idea for a web or mobile product or internal tool who want it built to a fixed scope, phase by phase.
needs: A short brief or sketch of what the app should do, who will use it and any systems it must connect to.

startup.headline: From idea to a working product your first customers can use.
startup.scenario: A founding team has validated an idea but has no engineers free to build it. We agree a small first release, design the key screens, build it in weekly stages and launch it on infrastructure that will not need rebuilding when you grow.
deliverables: A one-page scope of the first release, and what waits for later
Clickable designs for the key screens, agreed before building starts
A web app, mobile app or both, with login, a database and an admin view
Automated tests and a deployment pipeline from the first week
Hosting, monitoring and backups set up in your own cloud account
Source code and a handover guide, so you can hire developers later
startup.fit: Founders and early teams who want a minimum viable product built quickly, with a clean base to grow from.
startup.needs: A short brief or sketch, an idea of your first users and any must-have integrations such as payments or email.
startup.priceNote: Smaller: one platform, a few screens and standard login. Larger: web and mobile together, payments, many integrations or complex roles and permissions.

research.headline: Research tools and portals built around how your group works.
research.scenario: A research group tracks samples, runs and results in spreadsheets, and sharing data with collaborators is slow. We build a simple web application that captures the data, controls who can see it and connects to the group's compute and storage.
deliverables: A written scope agreed with the people who will use the tool
A web application for data entry, search and sharing between collaborators
Login and permissions that fit your group, including outside collaborators
Connection to your storage, cluster or existing data sources
Export of results in the formats your group already uses
Documentation so a future student or postdoc can maintain it
research.fit: Research groups and labs that need a custom tool for data capture, sharing or analysis, and want it maintainable after the project.
research.needs: A description of your current workflow, example data and who needs access.
research.priceNote: Smaller: one workflow and a handful of users. Larger: several data sources, a cluster connection or detailed access rules.

regulated.headline: Business applications built with your data and access rules in mind.
regulated.scenario: A professional firm handles client matters through email and shared folders, and wants a secure portal and internal tool. We build the application so that data stays in your environment, access is logged and every change is recorded.
deliverables: A written scope that records data handling and access requirements
A web application or client portal with role-based access
Audit logging of who viewed or changed what, and when
Hosting inside your own cloud account or on your own servers
Encrypted storage and backups, with a documented recovery step
A handover guide and a security note for your own reviewers
regulated.fit: Law, health, finance and other firms that handle sensitive client data and need a portal or internal tool they control.
regulated.needs: Your data and access requirements, where data must be hosted and any review process we must follow.
regulated.priceNote: Smaller: one portal and a small set of roles. Larger: several user types, document handling, integrations or detailed audit reporting. We build to your requirements, but compliance itself stays your responsibility.

msp.headline: Extra build capacity for the software your clients ask you for.
msp.scenario: An IT provider is asked by clients for custom apps and integrations that sit outside its team's skills. We act as your build partner: we scope, build and hand over the software, and you stay the point of contact for the client.
deliverables: A scope you can put in front of your client, in your own branding if you wish
A web or mobile application built to the agreed scope in weekly stages
Deployment to your client's environment, or yours
Source code, documentation and a handover session for your engineers
A clear support option for after launch
Confidentiality terms that protect your client relationship
msp.fit: IT providers and agencies that want to say yes to client software requests without hiring a developer for each one.
msp.needs: The client's brief, your preferred hosting and any rules about branding and communication.
msp.priceNote: Smaller: one clear internal tool. Larger: customer-facing apps, several integrations or ongoing change requests.
